html:
The Harakbut are an Indigenous people of the Madre de Dios region in southeastern Peru, in the forests below the eastern slopes of the Andes. They speak Harakbut languages, which are not clearly related to any other family. Their groups include the Amarakaeri, Wachipaeri and Arasaeri.

They lived by farming forest gardens, hunting and fishing. The Amazon rubber boom around 1900 brought slavers and epidemics that killed most of them, and survivors were gathered at Dominican missions in the mid 1900s. Since the 1980s gold mining along the rivers has damaged their land with mercury. The Amarakaeri Communal Reserve was set up in 2002 to protect part of their territory. Their neighbours include the Matsigenka and the Tacana.
